steps.title: Prepare GEM master mix
steps.instruction: Calculate the number of cells to load, then on ice combine RT Reagent B (18.8 µL), Template Switch Oligo (2.4 µL), Reducing Agent B (2.0 µL) and RT Enzyme B (8.7 µL) for a total of 31.9 µL per 1× reaction; pipette‑mix each reagent before adding to the master mix.

steps.title: Add glycerol to unused wells
steps.instruction: Add 50 % glycerol solution to each unused well of the Next GEM Chip G: 70 µL to row 1, 50 µL to row 2 and 45 µL to row 3.

steps.title: Load chip and run Chromium
steps.instruction: Mix the pDC suspension with the GEM master mix and nuclease‑free water as instructed in the 10× Genomics manual, then load 70 µL of this mixture into row 1, 50 µL of vortexed Gel Beads into row 2, and 45 µL of Partitioning Oil into row 3 of the Next GEM Chip G. Attach the GEM gasket, place the chip in the Chromium Controller and run the program.

steps.title: Recover GEMs and RT incubation
steps.instruction: After the run, tilt the chip 45° and gently aspirate 100 µL GEM from row 3 into labeled tubes. Add 125 µL Recovery Agent at room temperature, incubate 2 min (or until two liquid layers appear). Carefully discard the 125 µL pink Recovery Agent/Partitioning Oil from the bottom without disturbing the aqueous phase. Transfer the aqueous sample to a 45 °C incubator (e.g., Bio‑Rad) and run the RT program: 53 °C for 45 min, 85 °C for 5 min, then hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Dynabeads cDNA cleanup
steps.instruction: Prepare Dynabeads Cleanup Mix per 1× reaction: Cleanup buffer 182 µL, Dynabeads MyOne silane 8 µL, Reducing Agent B 5 µL, nuclease‑free water 5 µL (total 200 µL). Vortex, add 200 µL to each sample, mix and incubate 10 min at room temperature. Place on a magnet, discard supernatant, wash the bead pellet twice with 300 µL 80 % ethanol, then air‑dry.

steps.title: Elute cDNA
steps.instruction: Prepare Elution Solution I (1×): Buffer EB 98 µL, 10 % Tween 20 10 µL, Reducing Agent B 1 µL (total 100 µL). Add 35.5 µL of this solution to the bead pellet, pipette‑mix, and incubate 2 min at room temperature. Transfer 35 µL eluate to a new tube strip.

steps.title: cDNA amplification
steps.instruction: Prepare cDNA Amplification Reaction Mix (1×): Amp mix 50 µL, Feature cDNA Primers 3 µL (total 100 µL). Add 65 µL of this mix to the 35 µL eluate, pipette‑mix, briefly centrifuge, and run the thermal‑cycler program (per 10× manual, 11–12 cycles): 98 °C 3 min, 29 °C 15 s, 36 °C 20 s, 47 °C 1 min, then 5 cycles of 67 °C 1 min, finish with 74 °C hold. Store at 4 °C (up to 72 h) or –20 °C (≤1 week) if not proceeding immediately.

steps.title: Post‑amplification SPRIselect cleanup
steps.instruction: Vortex SPRIselect reagent, add 60 µL to each amplified sample, mix and incubate 5 min at room temperature. Place on a high‑strength magnet until clear, discard supernatant, wash bead pellet twice with 200 µL 80 % ethanol (30 s each), air‑dry, then add 40.5 µL Buffer EB, mix and incubate 2 min. Place on magnet, transfer 40 µL eluate to a new strip. Run 1 µL (1:10 diluted) on an Agilent Bioanalyzer High‑Sensitivity chip and verify cDNA concentration before proceeding.

steps.title: Fragmentation and end repair
steps.instruction: Use only 10 µL of the cDNA (store remaining 30 µL at –20 °C). Prepare Fragmentation Mix (1×): Fragmentation Buffer 5 µL, Fragmentation Enzyme 10 µL (total 15 µL). Add 25 µL Buffer EB to each 10 µL cDNA, then 15 µL Fragmentation Mix, pipette‑mix, briefly centrifuge. Run thermal‑cycler: pre‑cool 4 °C hold, 32 °C 5 min (fragmentation), 65 °C 30 min (end‑repair & A‑tailing), then hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Size selection after fragmentation
steps.instruction: Vortex SPRIselect, add 30 µL to each fragmented sample, incubate 5 min at room temperature, place on high‑strength magnet, and transfer 75 µL supernatant to new tubes. Add 10 µL SPRIselect, incubate 5 min, magnet, discard 80 µL supernatant (retain beads). Wash beads twice with 125 µL 80 % ethanol (30 s each), air‑dry, add 50.5 µL Buffer EB, incubate 2 min, magnet, transfer 50 µL eluate to new tubes.

steps.title: Adaptor ligation
steps.instruction: Prepare Adaptor Ligation Mix (1×): Ligation buffer 20 µL, DNA Ligase 10 µL, Adaptor Oligos 20 µL (total 50 µL). Add 50 µL of this mix to each 50 µL sample, pipette‑mix, and run thermal‑cycler: 12 °C 15 min, then hold at 24 °C.

steps.title: Post‑ligation cleanup
steps.instruction: Add 80 µL SPRIselect to each ligation reaction, mix, incubate 5 min, place on high‑strength magnet, discard supernatant, wash beads twice with 200 µL 80 % ethanol, air‑dry, add 30.5 µL Buffer EB, incubate 2 min, place on low‑strength magnet, and transfer 30 µL supernatant to new tubes.

steps.title: Sample index PCR
steps.instruction: To each 30 µL ligation product add 50 µL Amp mix and 20 µL individual Index TT Set A (record well ID), pipette‑mix, briefly centrifuge. Run thermal‑cycler (10–12 cycles): 98 °C 45 s, 29 °C 20 s, 36 °C 30 s, 47 °C 20 s, then 5 cycles of 67 °C 1 min, finish with 74 °C hold.

steps.title: Post‑PCR double‑sided size selection
steps.instruction: Add 60 µL SPRIselect to each PCR reaction, mix, incubate 5 min, magnet, transfer 150 µL supernatant to new tubes. Add 20 µL SPRIselect, mix, incubate 5 min, magnet, discard 165 µL supernatant, wash bead pellet twice with 200 µL 80 % ethanol (30 s each), place on low‑strength magnet, add 35.5 µL Buffer EB, incubate 2 min, magnet, transfer 35 µL to new tubes (this is the final library).

steps.title: Final library QC
steps.instruction: Run 1 µL of the final library (1:10 diluted) on an Agilent Bioanalyzer High‑Sensitivity chip; determine average fragment size for downstream quantification.

steps.title: Sequencing
steps.instruction: Submit libraries for Illumina NovaSeq 6000 sequencing (100‑cycle cartridge) aiming for ≥50,000 reads per cell. Alternative sequencing providers may be used.

steps.title: Align reads with Cell Ranger
steps.instruction: Run Cell Ranger v3.1.0 (10× Genomics) count pipeline on each sample’s raw FASTQ files against the human reference genome GRCh38 to generate cell‑gene count matrices.

steps.title: Initial QC and doublet removal
steps.instruction: Load count matrices into R (v4.0.3) with Seurat. Discard cells with >5 % mitochondrial gene expression. Install and run DoubletFinder (default parameters: PCs 1‑10, pN 0.25, pK 0.09, expected doublet rate ≈7.5 % of cells, adjust for homotypic proportion). Retain only singlet cells.

steps.title: Integrate samples
steps.instruction: Use Seurat’s FindIntegrationAnchors on the eight samples (HC61, HC63, HC65, HC66, HIV112_V1, HIV113_V1, HIV109_V1, HIV103_V1) with dims 1‑20, then IntegrateData (dims 1‑20). Set DefaultAssay to “integrated” and save the integrated object.

steps.title: Dimensional reduction and clustering
steps.instruction: Normalize (LogNormalize, scale factor 10,000), ScaleData, RunPCA (30 PCs), RunUMAP (dims 1‑20), FindNeighbors (dims 1‑20), and FindClusters (resolution 0.5). Visualize clusters with DimPlot, VlnPlot (genes CLEC4C, IL3RA), and FeaturePlot (CLEC4C, IL3RA, LILRA4).

steps.title: Annotate clusters and select pDCs
steps.instruction: Rename cluster IDs according to marker expression (e.g., pDC, B cells, NK/NKT, etc.). Subset the integrated object to retain only clusters 0, 1, 2 (designated as pDC) using Seurat’s Subset function and set DefaultAssay to RNA.

steps.title: Re‑cluster pDCs
steps.instruction: On the pDC‑only object, find variable features (vst, 1,000), ScaleData, RunPCA (30 PCs), RunUMAP (dims 1‑20), FindNeighbors (dims 1‑20), FindClusters (resolution 0.2). Rename clusters: 0 → pDC1, 1 → pDC2, 2 → Exhausted pDC.

steps.title: Differential expression analysis
steps.instruction: Identify DEGs for each pDC cluster using Seurat’s FindMarkers with Wilcoxon rank‑sum test, t‑test, and t‑test with overestimated variance; report p‑values relative to all other clusters.

description: The protocol below describes human pDCs enrichment from peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), single cell analysis, and development of human pDC transcriptomic database from healthy individuals and PWH. Human pDCs constitute less than 0.5% of PBMCs2 and the percentage of circulating pDCs decreases during infection.3 In addition, pDCs are very fragile and a lot of cells are lost during sample processing.4 It is therefore essential to have adequate numbers of PBMCs to obtain enough pDCs for your single cells experiment. Performing dead cells removal prior to pDC enrichment is recommended to ensure that only live pDCs are enriched. Additionally, despite pDC enrichment there will be some contamination from other immune cells and cell death due to cellular stress. Therefore, it is important to perform appropriate quality control after sequencing and remove non-pDC clusters from your sc-RNA dataset. Development of pDC transcriptomic database should be done on sc-RNA dataset containing pDCs only.
